Now I can see more details - the tram and the "FRENCH" text partially visible next to "EPI" (likely "EPICERIE" or part of "French Bakery"). The key findings:

1. **Tchakalian Bros / 老大昌** was at the corner of **茂名南路 (Maoming South Road)** and **淮海中路 (Huaihai Middle Road)**, specifically at **淮海中路877号** (the original address).
2. The store was at the **southwest corner** of this intersection.
3. The name "Tchakalian Bros" was used from 1938 onwards, and Pierre transferred his share in 1945. The store still operated under the Tchakalian name until Joseph closed in 1959.

The photo likely dates to the **1940s** - the "TCHAKALIAN BROS" sign is prominent, the tram style and car (appears 1940s vintage) support this. It's after 1938 (when the name changed to Tchakalian Bros) and before 1949 (pre-Communist era appearance).

top_results.snippet: 国泰电影院位于上海市黄浦区淮海中路870号，始建于1930年，由鸿达洋行设计，采用紫酱红泰山砖外墙，属装饰艺术派风格，外墙以绛红色泰山毛面砖搭配白色嵌缝形成几何直线秩序感，顶部设置狭长凸面尖顶及旗杆构成中轴线。1994年被列为上海市优秀历史建筑，2005年获评“五星级影院”，连续十三次获“上海市文明单位”称号。该影院前身为国泰大戏院，由外商筹资兴建，1931年竣工，1932年1月1日正式营业，解放后更名为国泰电影院，“文化大革命”期间曾改称人民电影院。1993年起成为上海国际电影节指定放映单位，2003年改建为三厅结构，2008年实现全数字放映。2022年8月25日暂停营业进行设施升级，保留建筑历史风貌，新增无障碍专座及厕所、育婴室，2024年1月5日恢复开放。升级后影院设置三个杜比音效放映厅并缩减座位提升舒适度，引入多功能厅及餐厅“香拉廊”，新增海派中式风格公共空间，联动推出电影主题特色

{"url": "https://shanghaitours.canalblog.com/archives/2016/09/11/34307259.html", "status_code": 200, "title": "An Armenian in Shanghai: The Tchakalian family bakery - Hong Kong & Shanghai Tours", "text": "An Armenian in Shanghai: The Tchakalian family bakery - Hong Kong & Shanghai Tours Tous les blogs Top blogs Tourisme, Lieux et Événements Tous les blogs Tourisme, Lieux et Événements Editer l'article Suivre ce blog Administration Connexion + Créer mon blog MENU Tous les blogs Top blogs Tourisme, Lieux et Événements Tous les blogs Tourisme, Lieux et Événements Recherche Rechercher Connexion + Créer mon blog Editer l'article Suivre ce blog Administration Partager Publicité 11 septembre 2016 An Armenian in Shanghai: The Tchakalian family bakery Version Française After traveling to Yerevan Armenia this summer, I got extensive information about the Armenian genocide occurring from the end of the eighteenth century in Turkey to the early nineteenth century. During this period some 2 million Armenian people were slaughtered , walked to death and tortured by Turks and Kurd militias working with them. The peak of this period was 1915 corresponding to the rise of the Young Turks party in the former Ottoman Empire. This very sad episode is still denied by many countries which sometimes want to preserve their relations with Turkey.  Among the famous Shanghai merchants in the Former French Concession was a company run by one of these families having to flee the Turkish massacres. This famous brand was called Tchakalian Brothers and was held by Pierre Tchakalian and relatives. Located in many strategic spots in town, there were fine bakeries providing delicate cakes as well as prepared food. The most famous of the Tchakalian shops was the one located right in front of the Cathay Cinema, as original photo bellow shows, on today’s Maoming Road. For three decades of Shanghailanders, the Tchakalian Bakery was the indispensable stop after an afternoon of shopping on Avenue Joffre (today’s Huaihai Road) or a movie at the Cathay Cinema. It was somehow an equivalent of today’s Hediard in Paris Place de la Madeleine. When attending class at the College Municipal Français on Route Vallon in the 1940’s, author Liliane Willens recalls meeting two of the sons of Pierre Tchakalian, "one of them was rather good in sports she says although he was older than me". I long asked myhelf if there were some traces left in today’s Shanghai of the Tchakalian bakeries. Actually the former Tchakalian bakeries are still opened, except may be the one on Huaihai Road which is now replaced by Uniclo Shop. They are still called “ Lo Da Chang ” (老大昌) their original Shanghainese name and also propose western recipes like the fruit cake or palm shaped biscuits, actually tasting very much like the Parisian ones. The reason for these bakeries being still operating is explained in the book written by Pierre Tchakalian’s son Jean, who had his name changed into Chaland to sound more French. He writes that his grandfather Krikor had to leave his bakery in Erzurum in the East of Turkey in 1896 to escape the massacres led by the new Sultan Abdul Hamid against Armenian Christians. The family could reach Ekaterinbourg, in the Russian Empire which was less hostile to Armenian people. They stayed there for a couple of years, Krikor working as accountant to sustain the family. Then they could reunite with a cousin who had a flour mill in Harbin along the Chinese Eastern Railway . In 1903, Krikor’s son called Bedros was 24 and made his way to Shanghai, then a promising developing city. He got a job in a French company, Mondon & Co, which imported French fine wines and champagne. In 1911 however, he left Shanghai for France where his employer retired and later returned to Russia. There, he got married and had a first son. In 1917, the Bolchevik unrest pushed the family to head for Shanghai again. Bedros, now called Pierre, started his own business of bakery which became rapidly successful. The family extended to three more sons , who were all educated in French and Pierre received himself the French nationality in 1932. As his health was declining, he started an association with cousins, freshly installed in the French Concession. This association turned to be a disaster, ending with the sale of the company to Chinese debtors. Pierre died from illness in Shanghai in 1946 and in 1949, the business was naturally seized by communist authorities. Today, Lo Da Chang is still renowned among Chinese who often queue outside the shop on Nanchang Road for “Old Shanghai style yogurts”. While doing this, they also pay tribute to an once Armenian immigrant called Pierre Tchakalian! top_results.title: 荡荡淮海路：老大昌的来历 - 澎湃新闻
top_results.snippet: 1991年前，茂名南路淮海中路西南角，有一家上海著名的食品店——老大昌。 老大昌有两家，东是“老大昌洋行”（MAGASIN FRANCAIS D’ALIMENTATION），开张1937年。 老板为法国人查卡利，改名查卡利面包糖果公司，称“老大昌法国面包房”。 西头这家叫“老大昌面包房”，1945年转中国人经营，称“华商老大昌”。 1956年法国老板回国，东西两家老大昌合并。 文革期间改名“红卫”，1976年后恢复原名。 老大昌以法式面包和点心闻名，有鲜奶栗子蛋糕、奶油泡夫、白脱快双和麦格龙饼干等，奶油蛋糕获商业部优质产品金鼎奖。 张爱玲曾提及老大昌，小吃名噪一时。

top_results.title: 上海“老大昌”，上海人最爱的味道 - 今日头条
top_results.snippet: 上海“老大昌”，诞生于1937年的上海，是旧时许多上海人熟悉的西饼屋。 老底子饿“老大昌“，民国时期，离圣约翰大学不远，兆丰公园对过，有家俄国面包店叫老大昌。 张爱玲曾在下课后拎走些十字面包。 老大昌蛋糕和面包融合法式和上海口味，成为许多上海人的共同回忆。 现在的老大昌依然是上海人最喜欢的味道，淮海中路店浓厚老上海味道。

top_results.title: 老大昌（瑞金二路店） - 百度百科
top_results.snippet: 老大昌（瑞金二路店）位于上海市黄浦区瑞金二路43号近南昌路，毗邻淮海中路商业区。 创建于1937年，是上海首家法式甜品店，八十余年传承，保持国营经营体制。 主要提供冰糕、拿破仑、哈斗、鲜肉月饼等经典产品。 历史沿革中提到，老大昌是上海首家法式甜品店，1937年建立，现为城市漫游路线节点之一。 每天客流量较大，产品包括冰糕含核桃果仁、掼奶油、蝴蝶酥、牛油蛋糕等。

zmshao +订阅 文章 总阅读 查看TA的文章> 3 抢首评 评论 8 分享 扫码打开 手机搜狐网 无需下载APP 精彩内容随时看 上海历史上的有轨电车-PPY讲人文历史 2021-08-22 17:38 上海历史上的有轨电车 PPY PPY讲人文历史 3月23日 100多年前外滩的明信片上，叮，叮，叮，…有轨电车的声音已经在上海街头响起， 清末的南京路外滩，有轨电车正行驶着， 本文的内容与现代有轨电车无关，上海历史上的有轨电车是指存在于上海20世纪前后67年余，从1908年3月5日起运行，至1975年12月1日最后拆除的有轨电车系统。 阅读本文要注意三点： 1，与人力车一样，当时的电车是按照英国的交通规则靠左行驶的，所以当时全上海不管公共租界、法租界、华界，车辆一律靠左行驶。 直到1946年1月1日，用美国的交通规则，改为靠右行驶。 2，开始只称“电车”，并没有“有轨”的称谓， 1914年上海无轨电车出现后，为了区分，才称为“有轨电车”。 3，本文所指的“南京路”，仅指外滩~西藏路段。 即指现在的“南京东路”。 1945年抗战胜利后，将静安寺路改称为“南京西路”，才将原“南京路”改称为“南京东路”。 不同年代南京路上靠左行驶的有轨电车。 电，进入了上海还是比较早的。 1879年上海工部局工程师开始进行弧光灯试验，5月28日以10马力的蒸汽机带动直流发电机进行照明发电，这是上海最原始的发电设备，但成本很高。 1882年，工部局采购了美国克利夫兰市生产的设备进行安装，5月在南京路51号创办了上海第一座发电厂，可供应16盏2000支光路灯照明之用。 在南京路、外滩至虹口招商码头，敷设6.4公里线路，安装了15盏弧光灯，7月26日正式供灯，获得成功。 虽然比世界上最早的巴黎北火车站发电厂晚七年，但比伦敦的电灯厂仅晚四个月，而比纽约的电灯厂要早四个月，比日本东京电灯公司早五年。 1882年在外白渡桥和礼查饭店亮起的第一批电灯。 这是上海南京东路江西中路口，上海第一盏电灯点亮的地方。 南京路步行街东扩后，重现了上海第一电灯。 但是，有轨电车进入上海却并不算早，足足又经过了20多年! 1881年（光绪七年）5月16日世界上第一辆有轨电车诞生。 当年7月得风起之先的英商怡和洋行即向租界当局提出了在租界内建设有轨电车的倡议（注：当时上海第一座发电厂还没有建成）。 法租界公董局就采纳了倡议，开始着手进行研究。 但1895年5月才有美国人亨脱向公共租界提出兴办有轨电车的计划。 但当时在公共租界纳税人会议上，煤气公司和自来水公司以“电车轨道回转电流会侵蚀煤气管和自来水管”为由，表示反对而作此议搁浅。 后来又有多次提议，都未获准。 1896年法国人罗发（A Rouffart）提出在上海创办电车的申请，并详细列出创办电车的利弊和保护地下管道的办法，这一提议得到通过，但上海没有一家公司具备创办电车的能力，工部局将上海创办电车的办法和细则编成说明书，在伦敦、巴黎、伯林等地征求投标。 1898年两租界联合组成电车设计委员会进行筹划，且在1899年10月一起联合审议了六家公司的投标，因意见分歧未有结果。 可以看出，上海两租界开始时，曾经设想过建设上海统一的电车系统。 1903年6月3日公共租界工部局单独与英商布鲁斯·庇波尔公司（Brush）和英国电气公司签订了合约。 但两公司并没有开始建设，因为他们注意到日俄战争即将爆发，决定放弃这一投资。 这是当时签订合约的主要内容： 直到光绪三十一年（1905年）工部局再次同英商布鲁斯·庇波尔公司签订合约，给于公司电车专营权35年。 而法租界公董局也与当年给于比利时东方万国公司经营法租界电车的专营权。 英商布鲁斯·庇波尔公司随即在公共租界西部赫德路（今常德路）附近（即现在7号线静安寺站东侧）购地12亩，准备建造电车车库。 同时将工程给美商哈泼兄弟公司承包。 这是1932年上海地图上和1948年天地图的英商电车公司 (赫德路80号) 第二年，布鲁斯·庇波尔公司又退了出去，工部局只得根据“转让办法”，将经营电车业务的权利转让给英商上海制造电器公司（Shanghai Eleetric Constiuction Co Ltd）。 工程仍由哈泼兄弟公司施工。 英商上海制造电器公司组建了英商电车公司，1906年4月工程开工，1907年轨道、电杆、架空线、车库等陆续完工。 这是英商电车公司股票， 关于道路工程技术：根据资料，1893年工部局已经开始试验用柏油、水泥等混合材料铺筑人行道，至二十世纪初工部局还自行设计制造了一台旋转式沥青混合料搅拌机，开始时使用来自美国的石油沥青，后来使用上海英商煤气公司获得炼焦残渣经过蒸馏脱水而成的煤沥青，用以铺路。 这样可以将电车轨道嵌入道路中。 电车轨道铺设工程， 这是南京路外滩铺设电车轨道的情景。 各种电车轨道铺设工程， 关于南京路的“红木马路” 根据记载，在道路建设过程中，早在1897年公共租界工部局分别从英国、澳大利亚、法国、美国获得了有关木块路面的消息。 在1906年铺设电车轨道时，第一条用澳大利亚铁黎木块铺设的路面（试验性）出现在江西路口以西约100多米的南京路上。 当时就引起了拥有南京路两侧的近一半地产的 哈同 的兴趣，据说哈同愿意出资将南京路建成“红木马路”（有关哈同出资铺设南京路红木马路的传说，网上的内容与实际有出入）。 1910年4月（南京路电车早已通车），工部局为铺筑澳大利亚硬木道路进行招标（用哈同的资金），最后怡和洋行以每千块澳大利亚赤桉木57银两的报价中标，次年2月怡和洋行将28万块澳大利亚硬木运到上海，经过在华氏200°温度下涂上柏油，铺在南京路西段。 昂贵的硬木路面耐摩擦，不用维修，成为租界道路的一大景观。 这条硬木马路从南京路江西路口向西铺起，一直铺到贵州路，根据记载，东端是铁黎木，后来是赤桉木。 1932年南京路照片 上永安大楼前，旁边的19层高的新永安大楼正开始兴建。 南京路的硬质木地面仍清晰可见， 铁黎木，原产于澳洲，是桉树的一种，呈赤褐色，坚硬耐磨。 但铺路后，保养比较麻烦，后来有了柏油和混凝土发明后，南京东路的铁黎木、赤桉木路面大约在40年代拆去了。 这是现在上海历史博物馆《近代市政建设》部分展出两块铁黎木。 第一辆电车从英国运抵上海，装卸入车库的情景 上海电车公司管理层，在第一辆电车前合影 在建设电车轨道时，为了将电车线路铺设到苏州河以北，还造了两座桥。 它们是现在上海历史上的有轨电车留下的最醒目的遗迹。 外白渡桥 外白渡桥曾经有过三座，第一座是由威尔斯等人1856年建的“威尔斯”桥。 木桥，桥长137.25米，宽7.015米，中间设活动桥面，船只驶过时须起吊。 因对华人过桥收取“过桥税”引起公愤。 工部局迫于众怒难犯，于1876年在威尔斯桥外侧造了另一座木桥，过桥免费。 因靠近旁边的外滩公园，称为“公园桥”，而因免费，老百姓称它为“外白渡桥”。 “威尔斯”桥被拆除。 公园桥建成后，车流量、人流量很大。 工部局在1889年6月进行了3天（每天8点~20点）的车流人流统计。 三天总数为：马车1633辆，人力车20958辆，货车22辆，小车（独轮车）2759辆，轿子27乘。 步...", Let me reassess. The key issue is that the photo shows a **tram** on the street. The Tchakalian Bros main store was on Huaihai Middle Road (Joffre Road) in the French Concession. The French Concession DID have tram lines on Joffre Road. However, the billboard mentions 上海光陸大戲院 which was at Huqiu Road (虎丘路) near the Bund area - but that's just an advertisement, not necessarily indicating the location.

The photo shows a wide avenue with tram tracks and colonial architecture with arcaded sidewalks. The Tchakalian Bros store had multiple branches by 1936. But the main one was at Huaihai/Maoming intersection. Let me also consider that one source mentioned "老大昌" had branches, and the sign says "上海光陸大戲房國際" which seems to be an ad for a movie theater's film projection equipment rather than the theater itself.

Let me look more carefully at the billboard text and try to identify if there were branches on other streets.

top_results.snippet: 在上海人津津乐道的“海派西点”中，朴实无华的面包所在比重少得可怜，远远不如蛋糕等花式西点吸睛。即便如此，因为西点的流行，也让上海的面包品牌存在不少“百年老店”。以冰糕闻名天下的老大昌，1913年在上海创立时其实是一家法式面包房。当时由母公司设在法国巴黎的远东商业公司派员来上海创办，法语名为“Magasin Français d’Alimentation”（直译为“法国食品店”），开在当时法租界的公馆马路（今金陵东路）77号。中文店名就是——“老大昌”，寓意生意兴隆。当时主要经营西式食品和洋酒等，并承办停泊在黄浦江上的外国军舰、商船的伙食。1919年，老大昌的老板转手，霍芬巴赫（Hoffenbach）成了新的老板，经理同时也是合伙人是亚美尼亚人鹊格利（Pierre Tchakalian）。鹊格利接手后，外文店名一变再变，先是“Tchakalian & Cie”（“鹊格利和切”），1934年又

top_results.title: 民国上海吃喝指南｜文艺复兴：维持二十年的波西米亚风格咖啡馆
top_results.snippet: 文艺复兴最广为人知的地址是霞飞路795号。1929年，老大昌已经在霞飞路上开出两家分店，其中之一就在545号，另一家靠近今马当路。1929年老大昌在霞飞路607号（今茂名南路口）开了一家分店，不久结束了金陵东路老店的营业，607号成为新的总店。1929-1932年间，老大昌名下不再有545号分店，正好是545号这个地址著录了文艺复兴咖啡馆和万国棋会的时期。但实际上，这家分店依然存在，继续和文艺复兴共用一个店址。作为老大昌股东和主理人的Pierre Tchakalian和妻子就住在分店旁边的549号。

top_results.title: 荡荡淮海路：老大昌的来历 - 澎湃新闻
top_results.snippet: 老大昌与它对角的国泰电影院一样，一脚茂名南路一脚淮海路，门牌挂的是淮海中路877号。1937年开张名叫“洋行”，做法式面包和点心生意。后来老板为法国人查卡利（F.Tchakalian），改名查卡利面包糖果公司（Tchakalian Bros French Bakery），叫起来拗口，听上去吃力，遂改“老大昌法国面包房”。1945年转中国人经营，称“华商老大昌”。1956年法国老板回国，法国老大昌也转华商。1957年两家合并，店名仍为老大昌。

1. **Tchakalian Bros = 老大昌** on **Joffre Road (霞飞路)**, now Huaihai Middle Road

3. The main store was at **霞飞路 607号 (later renumbered 877)** at the corner of **Maoming South Road (茂名南路)**
4. The French Concession tram ran along Joffre Road

黄山茶叶店
以前老爸老妈单位发电影票，
展开全文
基本都是老大昌斜对面的国泰电影院，
所以跟着去看电影，
经常会去老大昌开开洋荤，
有时是一客冰糕，
有时是一只色拉面包，
就是一只面包当中夹着老上海那种土豆、红肠、色拉油、蛋清拌出来的那种色拉，
记得当时是2角6分一个，
米道老好，
一个吃下去还是蛮饱的。
偶尔，
老妈会买一个白脱蛋糕，
或者一个柠檬蛋糕。
现在的老大昌和其他一些面包房也做白脱蛋糕和柠檬蛋糕，
样子像，
但是口味远不如当年。
当年老大昌的白脱蛋糕和现在有明显不同，
要小一些，质地绵密，
口感要硬实一点，
白脱味要浓得多，
价格也不像现在和柠檬蛋糕差不多，
当年的价格要比柠檬蛋糕高大约1.5倍。
现在想想，
当年应该是经典的pound cake的做法，
pound cake之所以叫pound cake，
因为料很简单，
一磅面粉，一磅白脱，一磅糖和一磅鸡蛋，
但是料很实，所以口味好。
现在的白脱蛋糕，
白脱少了，还加了不少麦琪琳，
所以白脱味差了很多。
另外用了baking soda来发泡，
而不是用蛋清和糖来打泡，
质地疏松，
不像过去那么绵密。
当年老大昌挂招牌的地方，
现在是Uniqlo（优衣库）,
看了总感觉有些怪。
这里也是周立波在海派清口中
提到“元宵模子”吃咖啡的地方。
他们大多是吃软饭的主，
往往打扮得山青水绿，
在靠窗的咖啡座一坐就是一下午，
一块钱
一
杯的清
咖，
被他们吞吞吐吐吃成卡布奇诺。
现在老大昌搬到了淮海中路成都南路口
茂名路口的东侧两个角，
还保持着旧时的建筑。
东南角上由万象时装商店华丽丽转身的古今胸罩商店，
门面也翻新了。
古今胸罩商店
东北角上的国泰电影院
还保存着上世纪30年代Art Deco的建筑风格。
有一次去迈阿密，
看到那些Art Deco风格的建筑，
顿时想起了曾经去过很多次的国泰。
下一次回上海，
一定再去一次国泰，
看一场电影。
租界时期雨中的国泰大戏院
1953年时的国泰大戏院
2020年初的国泰电影院
当年的老大昌
有不少人认为老大昌前身是法国人开的面包房，
也有不少人认为是白俄开的。
实际上，
老大昌前身Tchakalian Brothers是亚美尼亚人开的，
只不过和法国以及俄国都有些关系。
Tchakalian Brothers是Pierre Tchakalian开的，
和他的几个堂兄弟们一起经营。
Tchakalian老家在现在土耳其东部的Erzurum,
靠近高加索地区，
那是一个亚美尼亚人聚集的地方。
十九世纪末到一战结束，
信穆斯林的奥斯曼帝国的土耳其人
对信奉Christian的亚美尼亚人进行种族屠杀
（亚美尼亚人是虔诚的信徒，
在耶路撒冷的四个区中，
就有一个亚美尼亚区） ,
这就是最近还在爆新闻的Armenian Massacre（亚美尼亚种族大屠杀）。
Pierre的老爸Krikor在1896年带着全家
逃到了俄国的叶卡捷琳娜堡（Ekaterinbourg）,
老Tchakalian在那里靠做会计养家。
几年以后又搬到了中国的哈尔滨，
投奔一个堂兄弟，
当时哈尔滨是中东铁路的枢纽，
在沙皇俄国控制下，
那个堂兄弟在哈尔滨开个面粉厂。
1904年，
老Tchakalian 的24岁的儿子Bedros（Pierre的原名）
南下来闯荡上海滩。
刚到上海时，
他在一家专门从法国进口葡萄酒和香槟酒的法国公司Mondon & Co.找了一份工作。
1911年公司老板退休回法国，
他也跟着去了法国，
在法国他把名字改成了Pierre，
听上去法国化。
而后，他又回到了俄国，
在那里结婚，生了第一个儿子。
十月革命后，
他带着全家又回到了上海，
开了第一家Tchakalian Brothers，
又添了三个小孩。
1937年左右，
Pierre的健康状况日下，
于是和几个亲戚开始合作经营，
从这时起开始扩张到几个店
（注： 所以很多地方说80年老店就是从1937年开始）。
据1947年的上海黄页电话簿，
有永嘉路Route Herve de Sieyes （估计是工场） ,
总店（main store）在林森路Avenue Joffre 873号
（注： 一直到80年代末，
淮海路上几乎没有变动，
而且编号规则也一样，
从东往西渐大，
南侧是单数，北侧是双数。
老大昌地址是淮海路877-879，
基本和霞飞路门牌号一致） ,
分店一在林森路781号
（根据这个地址判断，
应该是海燕食品厂的地址） ,
分店二在四川北路，
分店三在南昌路（Route Vallon）287号，
分店四在愚园路。
Pierre Tchakalian自己的地址和总店一样。
但是，合作经营以后，
遇到财务上的困难，
所以有一家或几家店盘给了中国债权人。
Pierre 的四个小孩全部接受法语教育，
他本人在1932年时拿到了法国籍，
上海解放时一家全部去了法国。
但是，他合伙的亲戚家大多去了其他国家，
有一个Joseph Tchakalian（应该是堂兄弟）一直留在上海，
在1960年前后去世。
在现在淮海路茂名路口（以前老大昌地址）的Tchakalian Brothers。
照片应该是在国泰门口拍的，
对面在电车后面的商店招牌
依稀可以看到TCHAKA，
剩余部分给电车挡住了。
应该是Tchakalian 一家在自家店门口拍的照
1947年的上海黄页电话簿。
有关Tchakalian Brothers的地址电话
在黄色highlights的中间，
总共有7个，
一个工场，一个总店，四家分店，
最后一个是Pierre Tchakalian 的私人电话，
但是地址和总店一样。

图中淮海中路、茂名南路口四只角，
分别为国泰电影院、万象时装商店、
老大昌和花园饭店。
经过二百，还有一家黄山茶叶店，

黄山茶叶店
以前老爸老妈单位发电影票，
展开全文
基本都是老大昌斜对面的国泰电影院，
所以跟着去看电影，
经常会去老大昌开开洋荤，
有时是一客冰糕，
有时是一只色拉面包，
就是一只面包当中夹着老上海那种土豆、红肠、色拉油、蛋清拌出来的那种色拉，
记得当时是2角6分一个，
米道老好，
一个吃下去还是蛮饱的。
偶尔，
老妈会买一个白脱蛋糕，
或者一个柠檬蛋糕。
现在的老大昌和其他一些面包房也做白脱蛋糕和柠檬蛋糕，
样子像，
但是口味远不如当年。
当年老大昌的白脱蛋糕和现在有明显不同，
要小一些，质地绵密，
口感要硬实一点，
白脱味要浓得多，
价格也不像现在和柠檬蛋糕差不多，

现在想想，
当年应该是经典的pound cake的做法，
pound cake之所以叫pound cake，
因为料很简单，
一磅面粉，一磅白脱，一磅糖和一磅鸡蛋，
但是料很实，所以口味好。
现在的白脱蛋糕，
白脱少了，还加了不少麦琪琳，
所以白脱味差了很多。
另外用了baking soda来发泡，
而不是用蛋清和糖来打泡，
质地疏松，
不像过去那么绵密。
当年老大昌挂招牌的地方，
现在是Uniqlo（优衣库）,
看了总感觉有些怪。
这里也是周立波在海派清口中
提到“元宵模子”吃咖啡的地方。
他们大多是吃软饭的主，
往往打扮得山青水绿，
在靠窗的咖啡座一坐就是一下午，
一块钱
一
杯的清
咖，
被他们吞吞吐吐吃成卡布奇诺。
现在老大昌搬到了淮海中路成都南路口
茂名路口的东侧两个角，
还保持着旧时的建筑。
东南角上由万象时装商店华丽丽转身的古今胸罩商店，
门面也翻新了。
古今胸罩商店
东北角上的国泰电影院
还保存着上世纪30年代Art Deco的建筑风格。
有一次去迈阿密，
看到那些Art Deco风格的建筑，
顿时想起了曾经去过很多次的国泰。
下一次回上海，
一定再去一次国泰，
看一场电影。
租界时期雨中的国泰大戏院
1953年时的国泰大戏院
2020年初的国泰电影院
当年的老大昌
有不少人认为老大昌前身是法国人开的面包房，
也有不少人认为是白俄开的。
实际上，
老大昌前身Tchakalian Brothers是亚美尼亚人开的，
只不过和法国以及俄国都有些关系。
Tchakalian Brothers是Pierre Tchakalian开的，
和他的几个堂兄弟们一起经营。
Tchakalian老家在现在土耳其东部的Erzurum,
靠近高加索地区，
那是一个亚美尼亚人聚集的地方。
十九世纪末到一战结束，
信穆斯林的奥斯曼帝国的土耳其人
对信奉Christian的亚美尼亚人进行种族屠杀
（亚美尼亚人是虔诚的信徒，
在耶路撒冷的四个区中，
就有一个亚美尼亚区） ,
这就是最近还在爆新闻的Armenian Massacre（亚美尼亚种族大屠杀）。
Pierre的老爸Krikor在1896年带着全家
逃到了俄国的叶卡捷琳娜堡（Ekaterinbourg）,
老Tchakalian在那里靠做会计养家。
几年以后又搬到了中国的哈尔滨，
投奔一个堂兄弟，
当时哈尔滨是中东铁路的枢纽，
在沙皇俄国控制下，
那个堂兄弟在哈尔滨开个面粉厂。
1904年，
老Tchakalian 的24岁的儿子Bedros（Pierre的原名）
南下来闯荡上海滩。
刚到上海时，
他在一家专门从法国进口葡萄酒和香槟酒的法国公司Mondon & Co.找了一份工作。
1911年公司老板退休回法国，
他也跟着去了法国，
在法国他把名字改成了Pierre，
听上去法国化。
而后，他又回到了俄国，
在那里结婚，生了第一个儿子。
十月革命后，
他带着全家又回到了上海，
开了第一家Tchakalian Brothers，
又添了三个小孩。
1937年左右，
Pierre的健康状况日下，
于是和几个亲戚开始合作经营，
从这时起开始扩张到几个店
（注： 所以很多地方说80年老店就是从1937年开始）。
据1947年的上海黄页电话簿，
有永嘉路Route Herve de Sieyes （估计是工场） ,
总店（main store）在林森路Avenue Joffre 873号
（注： 一直到80年代末，
淮海路上几乎没有变动，
而且编号规则也一样，
从东往西渐大，
南侧是单数，北侧是双数。
老大昌地址是淮海路877-879，
基本和霞飞路门牌号一致） ,
分店一在林森路781号
（根据这个地址判断，
应该是海燕食品厂的地址） ,
分店二在四川北路，
分店三在南昌路（Route Vallon）287号，
分店四在愚园路。
Pierre Tchakalian自己的地址和总店一样。
但是，合作经营以后，
遇到财务上的困难，
所以有一家或几家店盘给了中国债权人。
Pierre 的四个小孩全部接受法语教育，
他本人在1932年时拿到了法国籍，
上海解放时一家全部去了法国。
但是，他合伙的亲戚家大多去了其他国家，
有一个Joseph Tchakalian（应该是堂兄弟）一直留在上海，
在1960年前后去世。
在现在淮海路茂名路口（以前老大昌地址）的Tchakalian Brothers。
照片应该是在国泰门口拍的，
对面在电车后面的商店招牌
依稀可以看到TCHAKA，
剩余部分给电车挡住了。
应该是Tchakalian 一家在自家店门口拍的照
1947年的上海黄页电话簿。
有关Tchakalian Brothers的地址电话
在黄色highlights的中间，
总共有7个，
一个工场，一个总店，四家分店，
最后一个是Pierre Tchakalian 的私人电话，
但是地址和总店一样。

{"url": "https://researchomnia.blogspot.com/2024/12/italian-tripoli-libya.html", "status_code": 200, "title": "Researchomnia: ITALIAN TRIPOLI (LIBYA)", "text": "Researchomnia: ITALIAN TRIPOLI (LIBYA)
Thursday, December 5, 2024
ITALIAN TRIPOLI (LIBYA)
This month I am going to research the "Italian Tripoli", capital of Italian Libya from 1911 to 1947.
Italian Tripoli was the capital of "Italian Libya". During the early XX century the city of Tripoli was under Italian control for 3 decades, that lasted from 1911 until January 1943. Italians conquered the town of less than 20,000 inhabitants from the Ottoman empire and enlarged it in 1943 to a big city of nearly 120,000 "Tripolini" (more than half Italians), creating a vibrant and modern capital in north Africa.
The census of 1939 showed this population in Tripoli:
Town......	Italians.......	Arabs........ Jews........ Total
Tripoli...	 47,442.........	47,123......  18,467......113,212
Italian Tripoli was at the center of Italian NorthAfrica in the "Greater Italy" during WW2 (borders in orange color).With Decree of 9 January 1939 the four provinces of Tripoli, Misurata, Benghazi and Derna were aggregated to the Kingdom of Italy, becoming an integral part of the Italian metropolitan territory.
History
During the Italo-Turkish War of 1911 Tripoli was conquered by the Italian Kingdom. The Italian fleet appeared off Ottoman Tripoli in the evening of September 28, 1911: the city was quickly conquered by 1,500 Italian sailors, welcomed by the population (
https://archive.org/details/tripoliitalianal00mart/page/36/mode/2up
Tripoli inhabitants welcomed the Italians; p. 36-40). The huge jewish community of Tripoli was very supportived of the Italian occupation (
http://archive.diarna.org/site/detail/public/1784/
).
TRIPOLI ITALIANA: The Grand Hotel, built in the early 1930
With the 1912 treaty signed in Ouchy, Italian sovereignty was acknowledged by the Ottomans, although the local Caliph was permitted to exercise religious authority. Italy officially granted autonomy after the war, but gradually occupied the region of Tripolitania. Originally administered as part of a single colony, Tripoli and its surrounding province were a separate colony from 26 June 1927 to 3 December 1934, when all Italian possessions in North Africa were merged into one colony called ''Libia''.
Since 1937 the governor Italo Balbo started a policy of immigration of Italians (mainly farmers) who were called the Ventimilli and some of them settled in the area of Italian Tripoli (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N_jA9rzM1MsVideo of Italian settlers arriving in the port of Tripoli).
Fiat train "Littorina" at Tripoli station
So, by the end of 1937, the city had 108,240 inhabitants, including 39,096 Italians (according to The Statesman's Yearbook 1948. Palgrave Macmillan. p. 1040). At the start of WWII Italian Tripoli had 111,124 inhabitants of which the Italians were 41,304: 37% of the city's inhabitants. Additionally there were nearly 18,000 Jews in the Tripoli area. Indeed after the Italian occupation of Libya in 1911, the Jews made great strides in education and economic conditions: at that time, there were about 21,000 Jews in the country, the majority in Tripoli. In the late 1930s, Fascist anti-Jewish laws were gradually enforced, and Jews were subject to moderate repression: still, by late 1940 -due even to the partial rejection of those laws by governor Italo Balbo- the Jews accounted for a fifth of the population of Tripoli and maintained 44 synagogues.
In 1942 Tripoli -according to estimates of the Italian government (Istituto Agricolo Coloniale (Firenze); Ministero degli Esteri, 1946)- reached a temporary population of nearly 150,000 inhabitants, due to the arrival of many Italians from Benghazi and Cyrenaica who took refuge from the British army attacks during WWII. As a consequence Tripoli was in that year -for the first time since the Arab conquest in 643 AD- a city mostly Christian.
Fiera internazionale di Tripoli ("Tripoli International Fair") in 1939
Architectural and Urbanistic improvement of Italian Tripoli
Tripoli underwent a huge architectural and urbanistic improvement under Italian rule (http://www.fedoa.unina.it/1881/1/Santoianni_Progettazione_Architettonica.pdf Tripoli section: p. 54-59). The first thing the Italians did was to create in the early 1920s a sewage system (that until then lacked) with water & electrical facilities to all the city and a modern hospital. Also was started the creation of the modern port.
Furthermore, in the western section of Tripoli was created an industrial area in the 1930s, around a huge tobacco factory (called "Manufattura Tabacchi di Tripoli"), with railway workshops, Fiat Motor works, various food processing plants, electrical engineering workshops, ironworks, water plants, agricultural machinery factories, breweries, distilleries, biscuit factories, tanneries, bakeries, lime, brick and cement works.
Governor Balbo used to say that "We Italians found in 1911 a big village of approximately 20,000 inhabitants called Tripoli and now we have in 1940 a modern capital nearly ten times bigger and one of the most developed and vibrant cities of Africa". (photos of Tripoli: http://www.paolocason.eu/Viaggio%20a%20Tripoli.htm ).
In the coast of the province was built in 1937-1938 a section of the Litoranea Balbia, a road that went from Tripoli and Tunisia's frontier to the border of Egypt. The car tag for the Italian province of Tripoli was "TL" (Berionne, Michele. "Libia (1937-1943)"  Italian car tags )
Furthermore the Italians - in order to promote Tripoli's economy - founded in 1927 the "Tripoli International Fair", which is considered to be the oldest Trade Fair in Africa (http://tripolifair.com/tripoli-international-fair/ Tripoli International Fair brief history). The so-called Fiera internazionale di Tripoli was one of the main international "Fairs" in the colonial world in the 1930s, and was internationally promoted together with the Tripoli Grand Prix as a showcase of Italian Libya(http://cronologia.leonardo.it/storia/a1937f.htm Filippo Giannini: Colonial Italy and Islam (in Italian).
Italian Tripoli's Via Generale De Bono in 1933
Indeed the Italians even created the "Tripoli Grand Prix", an international motor racing event first held in 1925 on a racing circuit outside Tripoli that lasted until 1940 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KEtz-wzbs9YVideo of Tripoli Grand Prix).Tripoli during the Grand Prix was visited by the elite tourism of the world and had even some "fashion" shops (
https://www.pinterest.com/pin/187040190754209597/
Italian women walking near the Tripoli Castle in 1939).
The first airport in Libya, the "Mellaha Air Base" was built by the Italian Air Force in 1923 near the Tripoli racing circuit (actually is called "Mitiga International Airport"). The regular air services (with postal services) in Libya began in November 1928 with the first Rome-Syracuse-Tripoli air route, three times a week in winter, daily in summer, of the "Societa Anonima Navigazione Aerea (SANA)" airplanes. In the December of 1931 the "Società Nord Africa Aviazione (NAA)" inaugurated the Benghazi-Agedabia-Sirte-Tripoli line, which followed the coast line. With the absorption of the two companies from the ''Ala Littoria'' in 1935 the service continued on the same routes. From 4 April 1937 the Rome-Tunis line of Ala Littoria was extended to Tripoli; in 1938 the Air France opened a Marseilles-Tripoli line, then extended to Benghazi and Damascus. (

Tripoli had even a modern railway station with some small railway connections to nearby cities, when in August 1941 the Italians started to build a new 1,040 kilometres (646 miles) railway (with a 1,435 mm (56.5 in) gauge, like the one used in Egypt and Tunisia) between Tripoli and Benghazi. The city fell to troops of the British Eighth Army on 23 January 1943 and the Italian colonists since then started to diminish (the following photo shows a family of farm colonists with British soldiers).
Tripoli was then governed by the British until independence in 1951. Under the terms of the 1947 peace treaty with the Allies, Italy relinquished all claims to Libya.

The elaborate zigzag/chevron decoration on the minaret in my photo matches the Hammouda Pacha Mosque description better.

The original Ospedale Coloniale Italiano was in the Halfaouine quarter (el-Halfaouine) of the Tunis medina, established in 1890-1891. But it moved to Bab el-Fellah in 1900. The sign "OSPEDALE ITALIANO" in the photo could be from either location. The Halfaouine quarter is in the northern part of the medina, near the Sidi Mahrez mosque. The Hammouda Pacha Mosque is in the central-southern part of the medina.

Let me check which mosque minaret is closer to the Halfaouine quarter, and also look at the Sidi Youssef Dey mosque which also has a similar octagonal minaret.

Name of Monument:
Yussef Dey Mosque
Location:
At the entrance to the town on the
kasbah
side, Tunis, Tunisia
Date of Monument:
Hegira 1020 / AD 1612
Architect(s) / master-builder(s):
Ibn Ghaleb al-Andalusi.
Period / Dynasty:
Husaynid-Ottoman
Patron(s):
Yussef Dey.
History:
After the annexation of Ifriqiya to the Ottoman Empire in the 10th / 16th century the number of Hanefite-rite Turks grew constantly. Two Malekite mosques, the Kasbah Mosque and the al-Qsar Mosque, were then given over to the Hanefite rites. Then Yussef Dey decided to give Tunis its first Turkish mosque. The works were commenced in 1023 (1614) and finished one year later.
Description:
The
mosque
bears the name of its founder and is particularly interesting because, while preserving several features of the Ifriqiyan
mosque
, it introduces several architectural novelties in its layout and construction.
The prayer hall is no longer set behind a single courtyard, but framed with courtyards on the eastern, western and northern sides. Along the north façade, the portico serves as a substitute for the narthex in local mosques. An octagonal
minaret
rises from a square base at the north-west corner. At the top is a balcony with a wooden awning, above which there is a lantern turret with a pyramidal roof covered with green tiles. This octagonal tower was to serve as a model for al-Jadid
Mosque
and for the
Mosque
of Yussef Sahib al- Taba'a.
The mausoleum, or
turbe
, built along the façade, is the first example in Tunis of a funerary
mosque
where the tomb of the founder is associated with the place of worship. The tomb of Yussef
Dey
is built on a square plan and has a pyramidal roof with green tiles. On each face is a large central arcature, flanked by two storeys of sunken niches with flat rear walls. The corner columns set on both levels considerably lighten the mass. The white marble flooring is enhanced with alternating blocks of black and white. The date of the
turbe
is inscribed on the central arcature.
The innovations, that is to say, the U-shaped courtyard, the octagonal
minaret
and the addition of the
turbe
, are outside the prayer hall. The prayer hall perpetuates the classic layout of the rectangular, pillared hall with nine naves and seven bays. The central nave and the bay parallel to the
qibla
wall are larger than the others and, at their meeting point, form a T-shape in front of the
mihrab
. The columns are of several types but, apart from a few ancient examples, all have Hafsid capitals. The roof is of groined vaults. At the front of the
mihrab
is an octagonal-based dome with scalloped pendentives.
The only new feature in this oratory is the stone-built
minbar
with its polychrome marble panelling. Malekite
minbars
are usually made of wood.
View Short Description
This was the first Turkish
mosque
in the Tunis
kasbah
, built in the early AH 11th / AD 17th century. With its square plan and green-tiled pyramid roof, this
mosque
, which was named after its founder, introduced a new style of architecture. The innovations include a U-shaped courtyard, an octagonal
minaret
and a mausoleum (
turbe
). This type of funerary
mosque
, in which the founder’s tomb was combined with a place of worship, was a Tunisian innovation.
How Monument was dated:
According to the inscription above the main entrance to the prayer hall, the works began on 10
Shawwal
1023 (13th November 1614) and went on until 22
Ramadan
(14th October 1024).

La tradizione di prestare la propria opera alla corte beilicale � ancora ben viva nell'Ottocento. Molto prima del protettorato francese dunque s'incontrano i nomi di Bensasson, Boccara, Castelnuovo, Costa, Debbash, Lumbroso, Nunez Vais, per citarne solo alcuni. Molti di loro erano nati in Tunisia ed appartenevano alla prima ondata di livornesi stabilitisi nel paese. Altri provenivano dalle fila degli esuli politici come Mugnaini,  Spezzafumo e Cal�.

Furono emesse obbligazioni, organizzate feste di beneficenza  a cui si aggiunsero i pagamenti delle prestazioni da parte di chi poteva farlo, i doni e i contributi da parte dello stato italiano che tuttavia li ridusse nel 1896 (da una somma iniziale di 70 000 Franchi si giunse a 36 000, con l'obbligo di accogliere senza alcun limite gli Italiani indigenti).

trace.content:
Los panoramas de Street View en la medina de Túnez son principalmente de interiores de tiendas y terrazas, no de calles a nivel del suelo con vista al minarete. Esto es típico de las medinas donde Google Street View tiene cobertura limitada.

Ya tengo suficiente evidencia para confirmar la ubicación. El minarete octogonal con decoración en zigzag/chevron, arcos ciegos y balcón con columnas es claramente el de la Mezquita Hammouda Pacha en la Medina de Túnez. El cartel "OSPEDALE ITALIANO" confirma la presencia italiana en Túnez. La foto fue tomada desde la Rue Sidi Ben Arous mirando hacia el minarete.

Ahora necesito determinar el año. El Ospedale Italiano de Túnez fue inaugurado en 1900 y renombrado Garibaldi en 1907. Si el cartel dice "OSPEDALE ITALIANO" (no "Garibaldi"), podría ser anterior a 1907, o podría seguir usando ese nombre coloquial. La foto parece de principios del siglo XX por el estilo, vestimenta y calidad fotográfica. Después de la WWII (1943), la presencia italiana fue eliminada.

Voy a buscar si había una clínica o consultorio italiano específico cerca de la mezquita Hammouda Pacha.

The photo shows a narrow medina street with an octagonal Ottoman-style minaret featuring distinctive zigzag/chevron decorative bands, a conical top with spheres and crescent, and an open balcony. A sign reading "OSPEDALE ITALIANO" is visible on the right side.

Šiauliai streets tell their stories. Tilžės Street
Tilžės Street is the longest street in the city, extending from Ginkūnai settlement to Lieporiai residential area and reaching about 11 kilometres. The Riga-Tilžė Highway built in the middle of the 19 century did not change the previous city plan formed as early as in 1783. The route was built across the square to the north, towards Riga. This way, two perpendicular axes were formed in the city centre, consisting of the current Vilniaus Street and the section of Riga-Tilžė Highway, which became part of one of the main streets of the city. That section of the road was called Šoseinaja ulica (Plento Street). In the plan of 1852, it is recorded as Tauragenskaja ulica (Tauragės Street). The street was named Sobornaja ulica (Soboro Street) in 1867, when next to the already standing St Apostles Peter and Paul’s Church, the Orthodox church was built. This name remained until World War I. During the war, the street in the city territory was not long, but the Germans divided it into two parts: Mitauer Strasse (Mintaujos Street) going in the direction of Riga and Tilsiter Strasse (Tilžės Street) going in the direction of Tilžė. In 1924, the street became unbroken again and was given the name Tilžės. The street grew longer and its names were changing. After World War II, it was called Tarybų, a bit later, Lenino, and eventually, the name Tilžės was returned to it.
The Chocolate Museum
In 1913, Antanas Gricevičius, a former employee of Vilnius Chocolate and Sweets Factory, established the Sweets Factory Rūta. He bought a large plot of land in the city centre with a garden and a house where he set up a sweets workshop. The factory was founded with only five workers. A. Gricevičius made sweets himself and took care of product advertising.
In 2012, the Sweets Factory Rūta, which was attracting passers-by by the sweet smells of chocolate, caramel, roasted nuts and boiled berries for almost a century, opened the door of its old building to visitors. Namely here, in the old building of the factory, the Chocolate Museum of Rūta was founded.
The exposition of the museum does not only present the interesting history of the factory but also reveals the secrets and peculiarities of four millennia of chocolate consumption.
Julius Janonis Gymnasium
In 1838, first efforts were made to set up a gymnasium in Šiauliai. Two plots of land were purchased for this purpose. Landlord I.Vitkevičius agreed to demolish the abandoned Pašiaušės Jesuit Church that belonged to him and until spring of 1845, to take its bricks to Šiauliai for the construction of the gymnasium.
In 1851, the solemn opening ceremony of Šiauliai Gymnasium took place. From the establishment of the gymnasium until World War I, it was called Šiauliai Boys’ Gymnasium.
In 1946, it was given the name Julius Janonis. Since 1954, the gymnasium is both for girls and boys. In 1965, it was granted a status of a gymnasium with a humanitarian profile.
Stained Glass Saulės mūšis (The Battle of the Sun)
The stained glass Saulės mūšis is in the Concert Hall Saulė (the former cinema). Three of the second floor lobby walls of the Soviet architectural building were adapted for the stained glass.
The stained glass that is 3,8 meters high, 52,1 meters long and occupies the area of 200 square meters was unveiled in 1986 to commemorate 750 years’ anniversary of Šiauliai city.
It is an impressive and majestic piece of art, the first monumental work of art of such theme and scale in the country. The stained glass is dedicated to the fight of ancient Lithuanians, it reveals tension and dramatism of that fight. Visual and colour rhythm of the stained glass sound solemnly, like organ music.
The building with a spacious lobby in front of the audience hall and its three glass walls – one front and two side walls – determined the compositional structure of the stained-glass.
The author of the stained glass, artist Kazys Morkūnas aimed to symbolically and artistically give a sense to the Battle of the Sun, disclose fighters’ heroism, strength, and determination.
St Apostles Peter and Paul’s Cathedral
The monument of Renaissance architecture St Peter and Paul’s Cathedral is the city’s most striking landmark. It as if shows the visitor where the city centre is.
The cathedral does not only dominate due to its impressive height (the apex of the tower reaches 70 meters) but also because of its convenient and well-chosen location.
The construction of the new church started around 1617. It is considered that it was initiated by the Samogitian bishop Mikalojus Pacas, while the key sponsor was the governor of Šiauliai Crown Estate Jeronimas Valavičius. Construction works were led by the dean of the church, the graduate of Vilnius Academy Petras Tarvainis.
On October 8, 1634, the bishop of Samogitia Jurgis Tiškevičius consecrated the new church of Šiauliai. Thanks to these people, a meaningful epithet “the greatest in all Samogitia”, describing the beauty and majesty of the church’s architecture, was heard on the lips of the Samogitian bishop Motiejus Valančius in later centuries.
Interestingly, the church tower had a mechanical clock installed for the money of the city residents.
The image of the architectural monument of the 17 century slightly changed over time. Wars and storms devastated the church time and again. Every few decades the church was repaired, renovated.
Prisikėlimo Square (Resurrection Square)
The central square of the city is divided into 4 parts by Aušros Avenue and Tilžės Street. This is the place around which the city of Šiauliai started growing. For centuries, the square was used for markets, fairs, live trading.
Interestingly, this oldest square of the city, the heart of the city, did not have an official name for a long time: it used to be called just Market, Market Square. Only in 1938, the square was assigned the name Laisvė (Freedom). In 1948, it was called Pergalė (Victory). In 1998, by the
decision of Šiauliai City Council, the city’s central square was labelled Prisikėlimo (Resurrection) in the honour of the Resurrection District of the Lithuanian partisans’ resistance, to which Šiauliai partisans also belonged. The square symbolizes the resurrection of the nation.

Johannes Hauerslev (1860-1921) blev aktiv fotograf efter, at han havde været i lære hos sin hustru i deres fælles atelier. Han arbejdede primært med arkitekturbilleder og dokumenterede herigennem, hvordan de forskellige miljøer og brokvarterer så ud før de mange nedrivninger, som var en del af Københavns udvidelse og modernisering. I 1896 blev han belønnet med en medalje på Industri-, sløjd- og kunstudstillingen i Malmø, og i 1910 blev han udnævnt til ridder af Dannebrog. Foruden Hauerslevs egne fotografier rummer samlingen også en række reproduktioner af ældre fotos.

The heyday of the trade directory was the early twentieth century peaking in 1936, with around 320 directories appearing. After World War II trade directories faced growing competition from telephone directories, particularly for business and commercial use and by 1950 large scale production and use declined. About the collection This digital collection contains 689 trade and local directories for England and Wales from the 1760s to the 1910s, with at least one directory for every English and Welsh county. Suffolk is an East Anglian county of historic origin in England. It has borders with Norfolk to the north, Cambridgeshire to the west and Essex to the south. The North Sea lies to the east. The county town is Ipswich; other important towns include Lowestoft, Bury St Edmunds, Newmarket and Felixstowe, one of the largest container ports in Europe.
The county is low-lying with very few hills, and is largely arable land with the wetlands of the Broads in the north. The Suffolk Coast and Heaths are an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Paul lived in the town centre above a shop in Westgate Street, where his father was the manager. With remarkable detail, Paul has taken us back to the 1950s when there was a bigger mixture of large and small traders in the town centre and many more public houses. Paul recalls when St Matthew’s Street was a narrow single carriageway and a policeman on “point duty” controlled traffic at Hyde Park Corner. Also when the Feathers Hotel at the corner of Lady Lane and Westgate Street had a slaughter house at the rear and it was not uncommon to see an escaped pig in the town centre. My teacher was a Mrs Roper who was kindly, but firm and fair. “I did my share of standing in the corner. I then changed to Park House, on the junction of Neale Street and Fonnereau Road. Several of us used to meet at the Old Cattle Market and we nearly always had the same bus LNG 725, a Bristol single decker. Historic High Street Goes Digital
PRESS RELEASE
7/11/22
An innovative online project has just gone live on our local webscene.
Supported by Lowestoft Town Council and Woodworks Art Cafe, The Historic High Street Stroll can be found on community website Lowestoft Old and Now –
https://lowestoftoldandnow.org/full/stroll
Every building on the High Street appears, including several no longer there!
Using 'drag' or 'scroll' takes you along Lowestoft's Historic High Street. You'll see one side of the street, displayed in historical and contemporary photographs. Clicking on a photo reveals both its history, often including more photos, and what it is now. Scroll to the north (the top end) and using the Zebra Crossing image, you can swap to the other side of the street.
(1min video)
Lowestoft Old and Now is proud of this feature. It's a unique way of showing the High Street, though of course building on many past presentations of its history.
Historical information is constantly added, which where possible we check for authenticity and accuracy. There's also a 'Memories' feature, where viewers can share their personal recollections of an individual building.
All 180 properties contain historical information, including some on the Scores.
Photos are positioned as accurately as possible using GPS data. For example, the southern end, now Artillery Way, shows the alleyway between the buildings.
Cutting edge software
is used on some of the photos, altering perspective and angle while retaining spatial fidelity (we can take a photo looking up or down the High Street, and manipulate it, accurately, so that it looks 'front on').
Lowestoft Old and Now is a community volunteer-run website, which publishes local stories, features a unique local recycling map, and stacks of information about support organisations, like foodbanks, councillors, local shops, and an events calendar. It's always looking for local reporters, local information, and ideas.

answer.reasoning: La torre en la foto es la Белая башня (Torre Blanca) de Ekaterimburgo, una icónica torre de agua constructivista diseñada por el arquitecto Moisei Reisher y construida entre 1929-1931 para abastecer de agua al sotsgorod (ciudad socialista) del complejo industrial Uralmaш. La forma cilíndrica del tanque con portillas circulares, las columnas de soporte de concreto armado, y el diseño constructivista son inconfundibles. La foto muestra el entorno completamente sin urbanizar (solo bosque de coníferas) y troncos de construcción en primer plano, indicando que fue tomada al momento de completarse la obra, circa 1931.

final_answer.reasoning: The photo shows a narrow cobblestone street looking towards a distinctive baroque church tower with a multi-tiered spire and clock face. Danish-language signs on shops ("Frugthandel en gros S. Petersen", "H. Olsen", "K.G.", "HUSLEJLIGHED") confirm Copenhagen. The church tower is Nikolaj Kirke (now Nikolaj Kunsthal), whose spire was reconstructed in 1909-1914 by architect H.C. Amberg, funded by Carl Jacobsen. The kbhbilleder.dk archive has an identical view titled "Lille Kirkestræde. Set mod Nikolaj Tårn" with coordinates 55.67826, 12.57987 and compass direction 66° ENE. Modern Street View from the same position perfectly matches the perspective. The presence of the spire (post-1909) combined with horse-drawn carts and absence of automobiles suggests 1910-1920.

Lille Kirkestræde 1 og Nikolaj Plads 28 ligger på Lille Kirkestræde 1 og Nikolaj Plads 28 i Københavns Kommune. Bygningen er fredet og har en tinglyst bevaringsdeklaration. Bygningshistorie Byen, som i kilderne omkring 1043 slet og ret blev kaldt Havn og siden København (købmændenes havn), var anlagt i strædet mod Amager. Herfra var det nemt at komme ud til Øresund, en af verdenshandelens maritime hovedveje. Den oprindelige kystlinje og havnefront lå mellem Rådhusstræde og Højbro. Havnen lå her i læ af de småholme, der i tidens løb blev sammenlagt til Slotsholmen. Den oprindelige by var omgivet af voldgrave og havde én kirke, Sankt Clemens. Vestergade var dengang den vigtigste vej fra oplandet til færgestedet, der lå ved Højbro Plads. Bydannelsen og færgestedet var baggrunden for, at biskop Absalon placerede sin borg her. Sankt Nikolaj Kirke blev første gang nævnt i 1261 og var oprindeligt et kapel, opkaldt efter de søfarendes helgen, til brug for de fremmede handelsmænd ved efterårets sildemarkeder, der blev afholdt her på en stor, åben plads mellem Østergade og den daværende strand. Kirketårnet, som er fra 1582-91, overlevede Københavns brand i 1795, hvor selve kirken samt spiret blev ødelagt. Nikolaj Plads var indtil branden en kirkegård, og herefter blev den en handelsplads. Efter branden blev hele området omkring kirken efterhånden dækket af et malerisk virvar af lette boder og træskure, hvorfra der blev solgt alle slags varer, men først og fremmest fødevarer og navnlig kød. I 1843 foreslog arkitekten P.C. Hagemann, at der skulle opføres slagterboder, udstillingslokaler samt en vinterhave og en koncertsal på området. Det blev dog ved slagterboderne, der blev opført i 1845 som et trelænget kompleks. Det store kødmarked gik under navnet \"Maven.\" Hjørneejendommen, inklusiv sidehuset, blev opført i 1797 af tømrermester Andreas Hallander (1755-1828), der videreuddannede sig under arkitekt C.F. Frederik Riise (1863-1933) var en dansk fotograf, der i løbet af sin karriere også udmærkede sig for sit udstillingsarbejde, bl.a. som generalkommissær i 1922 for verdensudstillingen i Rio de Janeiro. Riise var både historisk interesseret og teknisk fascineret af fotografiet og dets potentiale. Derfor forstod han også dets historiske værdi og fik i den forbindelse lavet affotograferinger af Danmarks ældste fotografier. Samlingen rummer derfor både originaler og reproduktioner. Det er især Københavns historicistiske bygninger og de bymennesker, der passerede forbi, som Riise forevigede.

Johannes Hauerslev (1860-1921) blev aktiv fotograf efter, at han havde været i lære hos sin hustru i deres fælles atelier. Han arbejdede primært med arkitekturbilleder og dokumenterede herigennem, hvordan de forskellige miljøer og brokvarterer så ud før de mange nedrivninger, som var en del af Københavns udvidelse og modernisering. I 1896 blev han belønnet med en medalje på Industri-, sløjd- og kunstudstillingen i Malmø, og i 1910 blev han udnævnt til ridder af Dannebrog. Foruden Hauerslevs egne fotografier rummer samlingen også en række reproduktioner af ældre fotos.

This is incredibly revealing! The first image (hamming=14, very close to our target photo) shows **the exact same street** but with the Nikolaj Kirke tower covered in scaffolding during renovation. This is from the kbhbilleder page titled "Renovering af Nikolaj Kirke med Admiralgade og Laxegade" by Frederik Riise (1863-1933).

Key data from this page:
- **Location**: Admiralgade, Copenhagen
- **Coordinates**: 55.67721, 12.58257
- **Compass direction**: Nordnordvest (332°) - NNW
- **Photographer**: Frederik Riise (1863-1933)

The scaffolding photo shows the renovation of the spire (which was donated in 1909 and completed around 1912). Our target photo shows the **completed** spire, so it was taken AFTER the renovation - likely 1912-1927 (Riise died in 1933, his collection spans 1840-1927).

Our photo is taken from the same spot on Admiralgade looking NNW toward Nikolaj Kirke, but after the spire renovation was complete.

trace.content:
Interesante. La celda 1 (Aguascalientes) muestra arcadas similares pero es una vista más amplia. La celda 7 (Tepic) tiene portales pero la plaza es más abierta, sin rejas. La celda 8 (Sayula, Jalisco) muestra portales y jardín con fuente y vegetación que se acercan bastante al estilo de la foto target, pero no es exactamente igual.

Voy a buscar más específicamente. La foto target muestra un edificio con arcadas de medio punto en planta baja y ventanas con balcones en el primer piso - es un edificio de dos pisos. Podría ser una foto de Atlixco (que mencionaron con portales y jardín), o de otra ciudad similar. Déjame ver la foto de Atlixco y también buscar en mexicoenfotos.

¡Excelente hallazgo! La celda 5 muestra la Plaza Ramírez de Concepción del Uruguay con edificios que se parecen mucho a la foto target - edificios blancos coloniales con arcadas y balcones. Sin embargo, comparando más cuidadosamente: la foto target muestra rejas perimetrales de hierro que rodean la plaza, lo cual NO veo en las fotos de la Plaza Ramírez. También, la celda 2 muestra la Plaza Ramírez con un obelisco/pirámide prominente en el centro, que tampoco aparece en la foto target.

Necesito buscar otra plaza. Pero el estilo arquitectónico es definitivamente entrerriano. Quizás sea otra plaza de Concepción del Uruguay, o de Paraná, Rosario del Tala, Victoria, o Nogoyá.

Déjame buscar la Revista La Ciudad que mencionaba fotos antiguas.

Las fotos fueron obtenidas por Cirilo Amancay Pinto, un jujeño que llegó becado a Paraná en 1889 para estudiar en la Escuela Normal, de la que luego fue celador y director. Las tomas, que quedaron registradas en placas al gelatino bromuro, le sirvieron para recrear la actividad económica, social y educativa de la ciudad. \"Las placas estaban guardadas en cajas de cartón que deambularon por distintos depósitos y terminaron en una estantería donde también había colecciones de armas y otras cosas que integran el patrimonio del museo\", relató a Clarín Federico García, quien rescató las fotos. El especialista sabía de su existencia por el relato de su madre, que había trabajado en el Museo Histórico. Y tras el hallazgo debió reunir información complementaria, ya que no estaba registrado el ingreso de la colección y se carecía de un catálogo que explicara el trabajo de Pinto. Advirtiendo que había varias fotos de la Escuela Normal, García fue hasta allí y consultó en sus archivos, lo que le permitió reconstruir parte de la historia. El resto fue obra del destino: García dio con un viejo cuaderno que Pinto había usado para registrar cada una de sus tomas, que también circuló por el edificio sin que se supiera su existencia. García inició el rescate de las placas con asesoramiento de la Fundación Antorchas y escasos recursos. Eso le llevó un año y medio, y otro tanto la conformación de una base de datos y la digitalización de las imágenes. Al fin, García logró dar con uno de los bisnietos del fotógrafo. \"Me invitó a su casa y me mostró otras cosas que habían pertenecido a Pinto. trace.content:
Interesante. La celda 5 muestra "Plaza 25 de Mayo" que podría ser de San Juan, y la celda 14 dice "San Juan - Plaza 25 de Mayo". La celda 4 muestra una plaza con obelisco y jardines. Ninguna coincide exactamente con mi foto target.

Voy a reconsiderar mi enfoque. La foto target muestra:
1. Una plaza con reja perimetral de hierro
2. Jardines formales con senderos curvos
3. Farolas de estilo ornamental
4. Una estructura tipo kiosco/glorieta con techo decorativo
5. Edificios de 1-2 pisos al fondo, estilo italianizante con arcadas
6. Sin monumento/obelisco central prominente

Esto podría ser una plaza de una ciudad del norte de la provincia de Buenos Aires, o del litoral. Voy a intentar una búsqueda más específica considerando que podría ser México (las glorietas con techo de hierro fundido eran muy comunes en México).

Un 3 de diciembre de 1908, comenzó la construcción de una plaza de toros en el terreno que ocupaba la cancha de foot-ball del Libertad Athletic Club.
El 25 de diciembre de ese mismo año, tuvo lugar la primera corrida, a la que asistieron 800 personas.
Luego de más de 20 espectáculos, donde se lidiaron toros de hacendados del departamento,
finalizó la temporada el 23 de mayo de 1909.
Un 25 de octubre de 1925, con gran solemnidad se inaugura el monumento a Artigas, obra del escultor Ezio Ceccarelli.
En la velada realizada en el Florencio Sánchez la Banda Centenario dirigida por Bruno Goyeneche ejecuta el Himno del Monumento, música del compositor Eduardo Fabini y letra de Luis Torres Ginart.
Así lucia por aquel entonces (Av. 18 de Julio, vista desde calle Entre Ríos, al oeste).
Acá cuando lo trasladaban desde el puerto.
Ésta de cuando lo estaban ensamblando.
¿Sabían que tuvimos un billete moneda propio?
Era de 100 centésimos o sea un peso con respaldo de un doblón de oro, emitido por el BANCO COMERCIAL DE PAYSANDÚ en el año 1863.
Más precisamente 1° de enero de ese año; por Ley del 27 de junio de 1862.
Por acá dejo salu2.

Puedo ver la Plaza Constitución de Paysandú en el Street View actual. La plaza tiene árboles grandes, un monumento central, y los edificios alrededor son de 1-2 pisos con estilo colonial/italianizante. La Oficina de Turismo está al sur. Los edificios al este tienen el estilo comercial bajo que se ve en mi foto target. Si bien la plaza ha cambiado mucho desde 1900 (se quitaron las rejas, se cambió la fuente por el monumento a Leandro Gómez), la escala y el entorno urbano son consistentes.

Sin embargo, no puedo confirmar al 100% que sea esta plaza. La evidencia es circunstancial: fuente antigua documentada, reja perimetral histórica, faroles ornamentales, ciudad mediana del litoral uruguayo/argentino con arquitectura italianizante.

answer.location: Plaza Constitución, Paysandú, Uruguay
answer.reasoning: La foto muestra una plaza ajardinada con reja perimetral de hierro forjado, farolas ornamentales, fuente decorativa, senderos curvos, y edificios italianizantes de 1-2 pisos con arcadas y balcones. La arquitectura y vegetación subtropical son consistentes con una ciudad mediana del litoral rioplatense (Uruguay/Argentina) de fines del siglo XIX o principios del XX. La Plaza Constitución de Paysandú es la mejor candidata porque: (1) históricamente tenía una fuente central ornamental que fue destruida durante la dictadura, (2) tenía reja perimetral y faroles decorativos según fuentes del foro SkyscraperCity, (3) la escala y entorno urbano coinciden con una ciudad mediana del litoral, (4) los edificios de estilo italianizante con arcadas son típicos de Paysandú. La foto fue publicada en mediotono (libro/revista), sugiriendo circa 1900-1910.
